title: do a code review of @backend/vault
description: do a code review and look for inconsistencies, non-idiomatic code, logical issue and edge cases

comments.author: Martin Czygan
comments.text:
# Code Review: backend/vault

## Critical Issues

### 1. Cache deadlock on expiry (cache/cache.go:67-84)

`Get()` acquires `c.mu.Lock()`, then on expired entries calls `Delete()`, which also calls `c.mu.Lock()`. Since `sync.Mutex` is not reentrant, this **deadlocks** whenever a cached entry expires:

```go
func (c *Cache) Get(k string) any {
    c.mu.Lock()          // acquired
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    // ...
    if time.Now().After(e.expiry) {
        c.Delete(k)      // calls c.mu.Lock() again -> DEADLOCK
        return nil
    }
}
```

Fix: use `delete(c.m, k)` directly inside `Get` (already holding the lock), or split `Delete` into a locked public and unlocked private method.

### 2. Division by zero in getFlowTotalChunks (vault.go:451-458)

When `objectSize > 0` and `chunkSize == 0`, the default branch computes `math.Ceil(float64(objectSize) / float64(0))` which yields `+Inf`, then `int(+Inf)` is undefined behavior in Go. The zero-size check only guards `objectSize == 0`, not `chunkSize == 0`.

### 3. Data race in Terminate (vault.go:909-913)

`Terminate()` reads `f.inflightDepositID` outside the mutex, then acquires it. Another goroutine could modify the field between the check and the lock:

```go
func (f *Fs) Terminate() {
    if f.inflightDepositID == 0 {  // read without lock
        return
    }
    f.mu.Lock()                     // lock acquired too late
```

### 4. Data race in Put overwrite path (vault.go:475-478)

`f.inflightDepositID` is set to 0 outside the mutex, while `finalize()` acquires and releases the lock internally. Another goroutine could observe a stale value:

```go
if f.inflightDepositID != 0 {    // no lock
    f.finalize(ctx)                // acquires/releases lock internally
    f.inflightDepositID = 0        // no lock
}
```

### 5. SendChunkWithBody body consumed on retry (vault.go:694-730)

The pacer retry loop passes `&wbuf` as the request body. If the first attempt fails with a retryable error (5xx or 408), the `bytes.Buffer` has already been read/consumed. The retry will send an empty body since `bytes.Buffer` reading is destructive.

## Logical Issues

### 6. Hashes are never actually computed (vault.go:264, 606)

`f.Hashes()` returns `hash.Set(hash.None)`, which means `hash.NewMultiHasherTypes(f.Hashes())` creates a hasher that computes nothing. The hash sums stored on the returned `Object.treeNode` (lines 548-550) will always be empty strings. The debug logging at lines 539-540 and 738-740 will always show empty hashes.

### 7. Variable shadowing of receiver `f` in Put (vault.go:504-515)

The `*Fs` receiver `f` is shadowed by `*os.File` from `os.Open()`:

```go
func (f *Fs) Put(...) {
    // ...
    if tempfile != "" {
        f, err := os.Open(tempfile)  // shadows Fs receiver!
```

This works by accident (the deferred closure only uses the `*os.File`), but it is fragile. A future edit could accidentally use the wrong `f`.

### 8. Wrong field in ModTime error log (vault.go:1025)

The parsing loop tries to parse `o.treeNode.PreDepositModifiedAt`, but the debug message logs `o.treeNode.ModifiedAt`:

```go
fs.Debugf(o, "failed to parse modification time layout: %v, ...", o.treeNode.ModifiedAt)
```

Should be `o.treeNode.PreDepositModifiedAt`.

### 9. Inconsistent Dir.ModTime vs Object.ModTime (vault.go:1136 vs 1012-1023)

`Object.ModTime` tries 5 time layouts, while `Dir.ModTime` only tries 1 layout (`"January 2, 2006 15:04:05 UTC"`). Both parse the same `PreDepositModifiedAt` field from the API, so Dir could receive timestamps in any of the same formats.

### 10. `int` truncation of file sizes (vault.go:499, 562, 578)

`objectSize` is declared as `int` (platform-dependent, 32 bits on 32-bit systems). `src.Size()` returns `int64`. The cast at line 578 (`size = int(src.Size())`) would silently overflow for files > 2GB on 32-bit platforms. `flowTotalSize` and related fields in `UploadInfo` should be `int64`.

## Non-idiomatic Code

### 11. Deprecated `io/ioutil` usage

- `api/api.go:22` - `import "io/ioutil"` (used at lines 194, 570)
- `iotemp/io.go:8` - `import "io/ioutil"` (used at line 53)
- `iotemp/io_test.go:4` - `import "io/ioutil"` (used at lines 43, 63)

Replace with: `io.ReadAll`, `os.CreateTemp`, `os.ReadFile`.

### 12. Regexp compiled on every call (api/types.go)

Six identifier-extraction methods (e.g., `ParentTreeNodeIdentifier`, `OrganizationIdentifier`, `TreeNodeIdentifier`, `PlanIdentifier`, `Collection.Identifier`, `Collection.TreeNodeIdentifier`) compile a regexp on every invocation. These should be package-level `var` with `regexp.MustCompile`.

### 13. Unnecessary `fmt.Sprintf` with constant strings (api/types.go:337, 358)

```go
re := regexp.MustCompile(fmt.Sprintf(`^http.*/api/collections/([0-9]{1,})/?$`))
```

The `fmt.Sprintf` has no format verbs - it is a no-op wrapper around a string literal.

### 14. `if err != nil { ... } else { ... }` (vault.go:420-424)

Non-idiomatic Go pattern. The `else` branch should follow the error handling without `else`.

### 15. Error comparisons should use `errors.Is()` (vault.go:290, 891)

```go
if err == fs.ErrorObjectNotFound {  // should be errors.Is(err, fs.ErrorObjectNotFound)
```

### 16. `http.Get` with default client (api/api.go:134)

`Login()` uses the Go default HTTP client for the initial GET to fetch the CSRF token, bypassing any proxy/TLS/timeout configuration set on the rclone HTTP client.

### 17. Doc comment mismatch (vault.go:178)

Comment says `NewFS` but function is named `NewFs`.

## Dead / Unused Code

### 18. Unused exported variables (vault.go:155-157)

`UploadChunkTimeout`, `UploadChunkBackoffBase`, `UploadChunkBackoffCap` are defined but never referenced anywhere.

### 19. `Doer` interface never used (api/types.go:193-195)

Defined but not used by any function or method.

### 20. `SplitPath` method appears unused (api/api.go:231-258)

Not called from any code in this backend. Contains a typo in its error message: "expected at least to path segments" -> "two".

### 21. Empty test functions (vault_test.go:163-167)

```go
func TestDeposit(t *testing.T)      {}
func TestFileRename(t *testing.T)   {}
```

These give a false sense of coverage.

## Minor

### 22. Typo in comment (api/api.go:52)

"when we except 0 or 1 result" -> "expect"

### 23. `context.TODO()` in Content() and several Get/Find methods (api/types.go:218, api/types.go passim)

`TreeNode.Content()` should accept a `context.Context` parameter instead of using `context.TODO()`. Same across several Get/Find methods that use `context.TODO()`.
